text: America's biggest port is 50 miles from the sea.
Why?
The city actually on the coast is little Galveston.
But in 1880, Galveston was the biggest city in Texas.
Why?
In Houston?
A muddy town on a shallow bayou.
So how did Houston steal the crown?
September 8th, 1900.
A hurricane hits Galveston.
The island's highest point under 9 feet.
The storm surge?
Over 15!
At least 6,000 people died, still America's deadliest natural disaster.
Galveston fought back, a 17-foot seawall, and it razed the whole city.
But the storm isn't what finished it.
Four months later, oil erupts at Spindle Top.
Oil companies wanted a port no hurricane could wash away.
So Houston dug its bayou into a ship channel 50 miles long.
In 1914, the president pressed a button in Washington, and a cannon fired in Houston.
Oceanships sailed right past Galveston.
Today, Houston, 2.4 million people.
Galveston?
About 53,000.
Now it's just Houston's beach town.
So, genius or just lucky?
Either way, that's why...
